notes.d4-date-named-page-file-format: The confirmed model decides it (SPEC §2.1): a pages-directory file whose effective name is an accepted date is the day, reached by every spelling of that day. Tine still reads it as an ordinary page reached only by its own spelling: a code bug under CM step 2, class K1 of the storeK part.
notes.n1-legacy-codec: Q-N1 ruled (D-20261103-CMA CM-NAMES (1)): the Legacy codec is OG's legacy-title-parsing, one decodeURIComponent over the whole stem, kept undecoded when any escape is malformed ("50%25 of 100%", "%E9"). No difference left. ("contents" -> "Contents" was fixed in batch 3, REG-CM-CONTENTS-PAGE-NAME.)
notes.n2-triple-lowbar-codec: Q-N1 ruled (D-20261103-CMA CM-NAMES (1)): malformed escapes and empty namespace parts now get OG's name ("%E9", "bad%E9", "lead", "trail", "x/y"). The one line left is Martin's deliberate difference: escapes that together spell UTF-8 decode ("caf%C3%A9" is "café"; OG decodes each escape alone and keeps it literal). tine-outline page_filename.rs decode_page_name.
notes.n4-org-file-links-triple-lowbar: A finding, not a decision (CM step 2 batch 6): `nearestLink` (follow link, Ctrl/Cmd+O) caches each block's link candidates per parsed AST (`candidatesByAst`), so after the graph's `:file/name-format` changes at runtime a block parsed before the change keeps the old format's page name for an Org file link. This test reads the same texts under legacy first, then triple-lowbar. Pre-existing; surfaced when this test moved off `pageRefsInText` (deleted). Fix: key the cache by the file-name format.
notes.n5-title-differs-from-stem: Q-N3 ruled 2026-11-03 (D-20261103-CMA CM-NAMES (2)): a journal is named by its date even with `title::`, a deliberate deviation from OG, which names it by its title ("Release day"). The model follows from round 9 on (store part: no difference left for this fixture); the `names` part still shows the OG-oracle difference, which is that deviation. The "launch walk" lines are declared, not bugs (CM step 2 batch 3, A7): page_identity.rs `launch_listing_walk` names a file by its file name as a provisional name, replaced by the answerer (`name_from`) for every file the launch reads; an unreadable file keeps the file-name name, as `discover_page_name` does, and is recorded as a discovery failure.
notes.n6-title-rename: The "launch walk" lines are declared, not bugs (CM step 2 batch 3, A7): page_identity.rs `launch_listing_walk` names a file by its file name as a provisional name, replaced by the answerer (`name_from`) for every file the launch reads; an unreadable file keeps the file-name name, as `discover_page_name` does, and is recorded as a discovery failure.

notes.o1-twin-*: O1 attribution lines ("owner of (page, key): model X, Tine Y") are the model's totalising fallback (path order) vs Tine's claimant order (SPEC 2.1); not a Tine defect. Harness follow-up: hand Tine's claimant order to the bridge as fileLe. Names part (batch 3): The "launch walk" lines are declared, not bugs (CM step 2 batch 3, A7): page_identity.rs `launch_listing_walk` names a file by its file name as a provisional name, replaced by the answerer (`name_from`) for every file the launch reads; an unreadable file keeps the file-name name, as `discover_page_name` does, and is recorded as a discovery failure. A non-owner twin answers None: its file's page is its owner's.
